                                  14            Plaintiff Apple Inc. (“Apple”) and defendant Guangdong Oppo Mobile

                                  15   Telecommunications Corp., Ltd. (“OPPO”) ask the Court to resolve their dispute concerning

                                  16   whether OPPO should be required to produce Dr. Peng for deposition, following his submission of

                                  17   a declaration in support of OPPO’s opposition to Apple’s motion for preliminary injunction. Dkt.

                                  18   No. 287. The Court finds this dispute suitable for resolution without oral argument. Civil L.R. 7-

                                  19   1(b).

                                  20            The Court denies Apple’s request for an order requiring OPPO to produce Dr. Peng for an

                                  21   individual deposition as part of expedited discovery.

                                  22   I.       BACKGROUND
                                  23            The parties agree that Dr. Peng testified in a deposition on October 30, 2025 as OPPO’s

                                  24   designee for certain topics in Apple’s Rule 30(b)(6) notice. Id. at 1. Apple did not notice Dr.

                                  25   Peng’s deposition in his individual capacity, although the parties appear to agree that Dr. Peng was

                                  26   asked questions that were not strictly within the scope of the two Rule 30(b)(6) topics for which he

                                  27   was designated, and that he answered those questions. Id. at 3, 5-6.

                                  28            Apple filed its motion for preliminary injunction on November 14, 2025. Dkt. No. 155.
                                         Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL          Document 315         Filed 02/02/26      Page 2 of 7




                                   1   OPPO filed its opposition on December 19, 2025, and Apple filed its reply on January 13, 2026.

                                   2   Dkt. No. 215; Dkt. No. 266. Apple acknowledges that this dispute was brought to the Court’s

                                   3   attention on January 21, 2026, more than one week after Apple had already filed its reply. Dkt.

                                   4   No. 287 at 3-4. However, Apple suggests that, if permitted to take Dr. Peng’s deposition, it would

                                   5   ask the presiding judge for leave to file an amended reply brief. Id. at 4.

                                   6   II.    DISCUSSION
                                   7          This dispute requires the Court to address several issues, including: (1) the permitted scope

                                   8   of expedited discovery and whether Dr. Peng’s individual deposition is within the scope of that

                                   9   discovery, and (2) if it is not, whether the deposition should nevertheless be permitted.

                                  10          A.      Scope of Expedited Discovery
                                  11          Although both Apple and OPPO refer to the “expedited discovery” permitted by the

                                  12   presiding judge, see Dkt. No. 287 at 1-2, 4, 6, their discovery dispute letter does not provide any
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   information about the scope of expedited discovery. Nevertheless, the record makes clear that

                                  14   expedited discovery is limited to the discovery needed to address Apple’s preliminary injunction

                                  15   motion.

                                  16          At the outset, Apple sought expedited discovery “to determine what additional measures

                                  17   [beyond the court-ordered interim measures] are necessary to protect Apple’s intellectual

                                  18   property.” Dkt. No. 38 at 2. According to Apple, it served “narrowly tailored” discovery

                                  19   consisting of “interrogatories (4 to each defendant), requests for production (4 to each defendant),

                                  20   deposition notices to Drs. Shi and Zeng, and a [Rule] 30(b)(6) notice to the corporate defendants

                                  21   (8 topics).” Dkt. No. 38 at 8. The focus of that discovery was to learn “the full extent of

                                  22   Defendants’ misappropriation [of Apple trade secrets and confidential information], and the full

                                  23   range of necessary remedial steps.” Dkt. No. 38 at 8. Apple’s demand for expedited discovery

                                  24   did not include individual depositions of any other witnesses besides Drs. Shi and Zeng, nor did it

                                  25   indicate that it contemplated deposing any witnesses who might file declarations in connection

                                  26   with briefing on its anticipated preliminary injunction motion. See Dkt. No. 38 at 8-10. The

                                  27   presiding judge’s remarks during the status conference on August 29, 2025 suggest that the Court

                                  28   agreed with Apple’s framing of the scope of expedited discovery. See Dkt. No. 48 at 14:7-14
                                                                                         2
                                         Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL           Document 315        Filed 02/02/26      Page 3 of 7




                                   1   (referring to “focused discovery sufficient to understand the full scope and breadth . . . of any trade

                                   2   secrets which may have been misappropriated in order to protect the interests of . . . plaintiff in

                                   3   this case”). Thereafter, the Court set a schedule for expedited discovery, including a deadline for

                                   4   the completion of depositions by October 23, 2025 (later extended to October 31, 2025). Dkt. No.

                                   5   41 at 1; Dkt. No. 90 at 3.

                                   6          At some point, OPPO served discovery of its own, to which Apple responded. See Dkt.

                                   7   No. 120 at 2 (“The Court has found no prior discussion by the parties or the presiding judge of the

                                   8   proper scope of defendants’ discovery, save for the competing views expressed in the parties’

                                   9   September 12, 2025 joint status report, which was filed before OPPO served any discovery.

                                  10   . . . Nevertheless, it appears that Apple does not disagree that OPPO may obtain some discovery

                                  11   on an expedited basis.”).

                                  12          After Apple filed its preliminary injunction motion, it made its declarants available for
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   deposition by defendants, and Apple sought and obtained deposition testimony or additional

                                  14   information from some of OPPO’s declarants. Dkt. No. 287 at 2. It appears that these depositions

                                  15   were conducted after the October 31, 2025 deadline by agreement of the parties. In other words,

                                  16   the parties seem to have agreed to expand the scope of expedited discovery beyond Apple’s initial

                                  17   framing to include matters defendants believed pertinent to their defenses, and they also seem to

                                  18   have agreed that discovery could be obtained beyond the October 31, 2025 deadline.

                                  19          OPPO does not argue that Dr. Peng may not be deposed because the deadline for

                                  20   depositions has passed. Rather, OPPO’s principal argument is that Apple should not be permitted

                                  21   to depose Dr. Peng in his individual capacity because, when Apple took his deposition as a

                                  22   corporate representative pursuant to a Rule 30(b)(6) deposition notice, Apple could have and did

                                  23   ask him questions outside the scope of the notice, and he therefore answered in his individual

                                  24   capacity. Dkt. No. 287 at 5-6. Thus, OPPO argues, Apple must demonstrate a “need or good

                                  25   reason” to depose Dr. Peng “again.” Id. 4.

                                  26          OPPO’s principal argument is not persuasive. Apple did not notice or take Dr. Peng’s

                                  27   individual deposition (even if some questions strayed outside the scope of a noticed topic and may

                                  28   not bind OPPO), and Apple was constrained at that time by the presiding judge’s orders and
                                                                                         3
                                         Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL          Document 315         Filed 02/02/26      Page 4 of 7




                                   1   admonishments to “focus” its discovery on what it required to file its preliminary injunction

                                   2   motion. Indeed, if Apple had instead decided to take Dr. Peng’s individual deposition, without

                                   3   regard to the topics for which he was designated, OPPO likely would have objected.

                                   4          Dr. Peng’s individual deposition was not within the scope of expedited discovery ordered

                                   5   by the presiding judge. However, as the parties apparently have agreed to take the depositions of

                                   6   some additional witnesses as part of expedited discovery related to Apple’s preliminary injunction

                                   7   motion, the Court will consider next whether OPPO should be ordered to produce Dr. Peng for

                                   8   such a deposition.

                                   9          B.      Whether Apple Needs Dr. Peng’s Testimony
                                  10          Apple’s principal justification for seeking Dr. Peng’s individual deposition testimony now

                                  11   is that he filed a declaration in support of OPPO’s opposition to the preliminary injunction motion

                                  12   regarding OPPO’s independent development of some of Apple’s asserted trade secrets. Dkt. No.
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   287 at 2. Dr. Peng’s declaration is based, at least in part, on documents OPPO did not produce

                                  14   until December 17, 2025, well after Dr. Peng’s testimony as a corporate designee. Id. According

                                  15   to Apple, because OPPO relies extensively on Dr. Peng’s declaration, and on new documents and

                                  16   information not previously available to Apple, Apple will suffer prejudice it if it is not permitted

                                  17   to “explore [Dr. Peng’s] personal knowledge of the documents” and his “new testimony.” Id. at 2,

                                  18   3. Apple represents that it will endeavor to schedule Dr. Peng’s deposition to minimize the

                                  19   inconvenience to him and to OPPO. Id. at 4.

                                  20          OPPO responds that Apple should have been well aware that OPPO would pursue its

                                  21   “statutory defenses” to Apple’s trade secret misappropriation claims, including that OPPO

                                  22   independently developed at least some of the alleged trade secrets, but that Apple elected not to

                                  23   take deposition discovery on those topics. Id. at 5. While OPPO acknowledges that Dr. Peng may

                                  24   be required to provide testimony as an individual regarding these matters at some point in the

                                  25   litigation, OPPO contends that this testimony should be obtained during “regular” discovery, and

                                  26   not as part of expedited discovery. Id. at 4. Finally, OPPO argues that requiring Dr. Peng to

                                  27

                                  28
                                                                                         4

                                   1   submit to a further deposition would impose a substantial burden on him, OPPO, and its counsel,1

                                   2   and that Apple’s plan to seek leave to file an amended reply following such deposition would

                                   3   disrupt the orderly procedure the Court has established for resolving the preliminary injunction

                                   4   motion. Id. at 6.

                                   5            The Court is not persuaded that Apple requires Dr. Peng’s individual testimony in order to

                                   6   respond to OPPO’s arguments that OPPO independently developed certain of the alleged trade

                                   7   secrets. First, Apple has already filed a reply in which it characterizes OPPO’s evidence of

                                   8   independent development as limited to two alleged trade secrets. See Dkt. No. 266 at 17. Second,

                                   9   as to that evidence, the reply appears to comprehensively address the evidence of independent

                                  10   development, and Apple does not indicate that it requires additional testimony from Dr. Peng or

                                  11   anyone else. See id. at 17-18. Third, in the joint discovery dispute letter, Apple does not explain

                                  12   why it needs to explore Dr. Peng’s “personal knowledge” of the documents cited in his opposition
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   declaration, or how his knowledge or lack thereof with respect to those documents bears on

                                  14   Apple’s motion.2 See Dkt. No. 287 at 2.

                                  15            The Court agrees with OPPO that Apple should have understood, even before it filed its

                                  16   preliminary injunction motion, that OPPO intended to assert that OPPO independently developed

                                  17   at least some of the alleged trade secrets it is accused of misappropriating. In the joint status

                                  18   report the parties filed on September 12, 2025 (Dkt. No. 59), two months before Apple filed its

                                  19   motion, OPPO stated: “Indeed, long before Dr. Shi joined InnoPeak, OPPO had its own

                                  20   voluminous and independent schematics and technical specifications of sensors including

                                  21   temperature sensors, ECG functionality and PPG sensors—features which are not unique to Apple

                                  22   but are ubiquitous in the category of wearable devices and beyond.” Dkt. No. 59 at 19-20; see

                                  23   also id. at 20 (“OPPO has no way of knowing what [Apple’s ‘unreleased products’] are and how

                                  24   they may differ from products that OPPO itself is independently researching or developing.”); id.

                                  25
                                       1
                                  26     OPPO states that Dr. Peng lives in Mainland China and would need to travel to Hong Kong SAR
                                       or another location to sit for the deposition, and his counsel would also need to travel to the same
                                  27   location. Dkt. No. 287 at 6.
                                       2
                                  28     There is no indication in the docket that either party proposes to rely on live fact witness
                                       testimony at the preliminary injunction hearing or that the Court will permit such testimony.
                                                                                           5
                                         Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL          Document 315         Filed 02/02/26     Page 6 of 7




                                   1   at 29-30 (seeking discovery of Apple’s development of its alleged trade secrets, because such

                                   2   discovery may “show how similar features might have been developed independently, or derived

                                   3   from public sources”). Apple did not seek expedited discovery of this defense prior to filing its

                                   4   motion.

                                   5          The Court notes that in the joint status report the parties filed on January 16, 2026 (Dkt.

                                   6   No. 274), after the briefing was complete on the preliminary injunction motion, Apple advised the

                                   7   presiding judge that its motion could be decided based on argument and the “detailed submissions

                                   8   provided by the Parties,” and that it “does not believe witness testimony is necessary” at the

                                   9   hearing. Dkt. No. 274 at 1. Apple did not raise the need for additional depositions, or additional

                                  10   discovery of any kind, in the January 16, 2026 status report. To the contrary, in arguing against

                                  11   holding an evidentiary hearing, Apple informed that presiding judge: “Every witness Defendants

                                  12   intend to call to testify at the hearing submitted a declaration and was deposed. Accordingly, the
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   Parties’ submissions provide a sufficient basis for the Court to make an informed decision without

                                  14   the need for live witness testimony.” Id. at 2. In that same status report, OPPO and InnoPeak

                                  15   highlighted that their defenses to Apple’s motion included “that Apple’s purported trade secrets

                                  16   consist of material that is publicly known, readily ascertainable, and/or independently developed

                                  17   by OPPO and InnoPeak.” Id. at 3.

                                  18          In short, while it may be possible to mitigate the substantial inconvenience and burden a

                                  19   further deposition of Dr. Peng would impose on the witness, OPPO, and its counsel, Apple has not

                                  20   demonstrated a need for Dr. Peng’s individual testimony regarding the matters in his opposition

                                  21   declaration for purposes of the pending motion for preliminary injunction.

                                  22   III.   CONCLUSION
                                  23   For the reasons explained above, the Court denies Apple’s request for Dr. Peng’s individual

                                  24   deposition as part of expedited discovery, without prejudice to Apple obtaining his deposition at a
